source.title: An Adaptive Policy to Employ Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Weisen Jiang; Hansi Yang; Yu Zhang; J. Kwok

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a gradient-norm sharpness proxy to decide when to apply SAM and reports training and test results for its policy. It does not test the claim versions’ specified interventions or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work for the association between gradient variance and generalization. Its own gradient-variance plots compare SAM and ERM, but do not test whether a magnitude-aware perturbation measure tracks the generalization gap. Table 1 reports test accuracy for SAM and ERM on clean CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; other method comparisons are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses a sharpness proxy to select SAM updates and evaluates optimization efficiency and test accuracy. It does not test any stated version. In particular, gradient variance and squared gradient norms are not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure, and the experiments do not rank generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their geometry-based adaptive policy reduces SAM updates while retaining comparable or improving test performance in the evaluated settings; they also establish a convergence-rate result and demonstrate integration with LookSAM. They do not claim every adaptive variant matches SAM in every setting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAM or ERM updates selected by a stochastic-gradient-norm threshold and compares that adaptive policy with ERM, SAM, and SAM variants; it does not perform the claim versions’ interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture, dataset, and the adaptive threshold schedule are varied. For noisy CIFAR-10, LookSAM performance depends on k; k=2 performs better than k=3, 4, or 5, especially at higher noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM has higher mean test accuracy than ERM in all eight clean CIFAR model–dataset comparisons in Table 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can improve held-out image-classification accuracy over ERM under the tested training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1 describes lower gradient variance under SAM than ERM for three convolutional architectures on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM reduces stochastic-gradient variance relative to ERM in these training comparisons.

record.problems: The clean-dataset table reports test accuracy rather than training-to-test gaps. Gradient-variance comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values. The paper’s statement about the gradient-variance/generalization association cites prior work; its own experiments do not directly establish that association.
record.rows_left_out: Noisy-label CIFAR-10 results are outside the claim’s natural-label scope. Comparisons involving AE-SAM, AE-LookSAM, ESAM, SS-SAM, and LookSAM are omitted because they evaluate the paper’s proposed efficiency policy or other methods rather than the claim’s specified versions.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy. Partial label-noise robustness experiments do not establish this comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. Adaptive selection of SAM updates is a different intervention.
Batch-size comparisons within a workload under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The observed accuracy gains and lower gradient variance remain valid descriptive findings. Their row states are cannot_determine with respect to the listed claim versions, rather than evidence that any version is absent or challenged.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, rankings against norm or margin measures, and the stated generalization-gap relationship.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
